title: Comparison of Spatial Entanglement between dissociated atom and ion : molecular ion photo-dissociated by sequential two-photon absorption and correlated two-photon absorption
abstract: We have studied the fidelity of spatial entanglement between dissociated atom and ion from two photon dissociation of hydrogen molecular ion H 2 + . Two processes for two photon dissociation of molecular ion have been considered (i) sequential two photon (STP) absorption and (ii) correlated two photon (CTP) absorption by the molecular ion. We compared the results for fidelity of spatial entanglement (FSE) between dissociated atom and ion for these two types of dissociation. In a previous study in our group [1] we have shown that when an atom interact with nonlocal mode of electromagnetic field (which has been derived field theoretically), simultaneous phase-correlated two pho1 ton absorption by the atom occurs within a very short time δt << ω , where ω is the laser frequency, and the rate of this correlated two photon absorption is linear in intensity. This will happen when the photon flux in the interaction region is high i.e. laser intensity is higher than 10 10 W/cm 2 . In this work we have extended this formalism to study the correlated two photon dissociation of molecular ion and to explore the effect of correlation between two simultaneous photo-absorption processes on the fidelity for spatial entanglement of dissociated atom and ion. Dependence of fidelity for spatial entanglement on the photon frequency has been studied for both the STP and CTP dissociation, to show that photon frequency can be used as control parameter to achieve maximum fidelity. Saturation of fidelity with the increase in time at which fidelity was calculated shows the robustness of the processes considered here. A scheme for detection of spatial entanglement between ion and atom has been suggested.
summary: This theoretical study compares the generation of spatial entanglement between an atom and ion resulting from $	ext{H}_2^+$ dissociation via two-photon absorption. By modeling both sequential (STP) and correlated (CTP) excitation pathways, the authors demonstrate that CTP mechanisms, enabled by high photon flux, yield significantly higher and more controllable spatial entanglement fidelity. This suggests using controlled light-matter interactions to enhance quantum correlations in molecular physics.
main_problem: The study compares the fidelity of spatial entanglement between a dissociated atom and ion resulting from two different photo-dissociation mechanisms: Sequential Two-Photon (STP) absorption versus Correlated Two-Photon (CTP) absorption.
main_result: CTP dissociation yields significantly higher and more robust spatial entanglement fidelity compared to STP dissociation, suggesting that correlated photon interactions are superior for generating entangled products.
method: The authors employed the wavepacket formalism to calculate the time evolution of the dissociating molecular ion state and subsequently determined the fidelity using second-order correlation functions derived from the relative coordinates.
model_or_system: The system under study is the hydrogen molecular ion ($	ext{H}_2^+$) undergoing photo-dissociation into a free atom and an ion. The comparison hinges on two distinct excitation mechanisms: STP (local field interaction) and CTP (nonlocal, phase-correlated interaction).
key_observables: Fidelity of Spatial Entanglement (FSE), second-order correlation functions ($G^{(2)}_{a1a1}$ and $G^{(2)}_{a1a2}$), and the ratio $\kappa = G^{(2)}_{a1a1} / G^{(2)}_{a1a2}$.
important_parameters: Photon frequency, time elapsed during dissociation, initial width of the Gaussian wavepacket ($	ext{WGW}$), and laser intensity (required to achieve CTP regime).
main_assumptions: The Born-Oppenheimer approximation is used for separating electronic and nuclear wavefunctions. The CTP process assumes high photon flux leading to simultaneous, phase-correlated absorption within a very short time ($\delta t \ll 1/\omega$).
figures_summary: Figures show the Fidelity for spatial entanglement as a function of $	ext{WGW}$ for both STP and CTP dissociation at various times and photon frequencies.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework by comparing the two absorption mechanisms (STP vs. CTP). It then details the calculation of entanglement fidelity using wavepacket propagation, culminating in a comparison showing that CTP provides superior entanglement control via frequency tuning.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses how quantum light-matter interaction regimes (sequential vs. correlated photon absorption) can be engineered to enhance fundamental quantum correlations like spatial entanglement in molecular systems, which is highly relevant for quantum simulation and measurement protocols.
